About Edconic
Edconic is a leading player in the alternative, experiential education space. We partner with the world's largest and most well-known brands to create and run schools that capture the legacy and value of each brand. Our students get truly unique, once-in-a-lifetime experiences that help shape their future and give them the skills they need to reach their goals.
The Role
We're looking for an experienced Front-End Developer to join our web team, which owns every Edconic digital property – from our school websites to landing pages and email templates. You'll work alongside designers, IT, and MarTech to build solutions that serve real business needs while protecting each brand's unique identity.
You'll be one of two developers on the team, working directly with our lead developer. That means real ownership of your work, a genuine voice in how we build, very little process overhead, and a codebase that is actively moving toward a modern, standardized WordPress stack. We value craft: fast pages and code that the next developer can read.
What You'll Do
Build and maintain public-facing websites, micro-sites, and landing pages in collaboration with our lead developer, IT, and MarTech.
Work with UX/UI designers to confirm the technical feasibility of designs, then translate them into polished, responsive pages that stay true to each brand.
Build and maintain custom WordPress themes across both of our stacks: modern block-based builds (ACF Blocks, core blocks, block patterns, theme.json) and established classic themes built on PHP templates, Advanced Custom Fields, and Sass.
Collaborate with our lead developer to shape the team's coding standards, tooling, and workflow, and help migrate our existing sites toward our new modern stack.
Stay current on emerging web standards and bring ideas to the table where they genuinely fit.
What You Bring
4+ years of front-end web development experience, with strong skills in semantic HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and WordPress.
The ability to build a custom WordPress theme from scratch using PHP templates and Advanced Custom Fields.
Strong CSS skills across Sass and modern native CSS (custom properties, nesting), and solid vanilla JavaScript.
Comfort working in Git/GitHub with pull requests and code reviews, and with npm-based build tools and the command line.
A habit of writing semantic, well-structured HTML that covers accessibility basics, with an eye for reuse, cross-browser compatibility, performance, and SEO.
Experience building and testing HTML emails.
Strong UX/UI sensibilities and a desire to sweat the small stuff.
A proactive, self-directed working style – you can run with a project independently and prioritize across several at once.
Excellent written and verbal communication – you're positive, collaborative, objective, and solution-oriented.
Bonus Experience
Modern WordPress block development: ACF Blocks, block.json, theme.json, and block patterns.
Composer, Bedrock or other Roots tooling (Sage/Blade, Trellis), Vite, or CI/CD with GitHub Actions.
Deeper accessibility experience (WCAG, ARIA, assistive-technology testing).
CRM and marketing automation integration (Salesforce, Pardot/Account Engagement).
Multilingual WordPress sites.
A modern JavaScript framework such as React or Vue.
UX or UI design, and design tools such as Figma and Adobe Creative Suite.
How We Use AI
AI-assisted development is a new and evolving part of our workflow. We use AI coding tools to speed up research, scaffolding, review, and routine work, and you're welcome to do the same.

Our vision is to build the next generation platform to enable easy and fast creation of audio and video content powered by cutting-edge AI. Building a revolutionary way to record, transcribe, edit, and mix spoken audio and video comes with a series of unique challenges and requires solving hard and complex problems.
As a lead product data scientist on the team, you will play a critical role in shaping our growth strategy, up-leveling our experimentation culture, and scaling our business.
What You’ll Do
Conduct in-depth analysis to shape product PLG motion and B2B strategy.
Develop deep understanding of the product ecosystem and identify opportunities to drive activation, engagement, and monetization through actionable insights.
Leveraging AI tools to build and maintain self-service analytics enabling stakeholders to access reliable metrics, size opportunities, design experiments, and interpret results independently.
Improve execution rigor of product teams by owning success metrics and opportunity sizing.
Brain buddy with product and engineering teams for day-to-day experiment design, deployment, and analysis. Provide creative solutions for tricky experimentation scenarios.
Evolve experimentation culture and practices within the company.
What You Bring
5–8 years of experience in a Data Scientist or similar role.
3+ years working in a growth function.
Strong business and product intuition to identify opportunities in the growth ecosystem.
Strong knowledge of statistical analysis and A/B tests.
Strong SQL skills and proficient in at least one programming language such as Python or R.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
Curiosity, savviness to navigate in a dynamic environment, and a growth mindset.
Having worked at a fast-growing start-up is a plus.
The base salary range for this role is $200,000 - $250,000/year. Final offer amounts will carefully consider multiple factors, including prior experience, expertise, location, level, and may vary from the amount above.

About ZoomInfo
ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute, you’ll make things happen, fast.
The Opportunity
ZoomInfo’s Core Data team builds the company and contact data behind the Go-To-Market Intelligence Platform: hundreds of millions of records, resolved to the right entity, kept accurate, and delivered to more than 35,000 customers.
The way that data is produced is changing. For years it came from deterministic pipelines: many sources, weighted and decayed, one winner per attribute. Core Data is now moving to AI-native data management, where an agent pursues the evidence for an entity, decides every attribute over all of it, and records why. The company and contact agents already exist as working, measured prototypes. What does not exist yet is the machinery that runs them at production volume, proves every version before it ships, and lets researchers and product managers operate them without an engineer in the loop.
We are hiring a Senior Applied AI Engineer to build and own that machinery. You will complete the entity-agent pipeline, build the evidence adapters behind a single envelope, run the benchmark and golden-gate system on a schedule, build the review and batch tooling the team operates, and carry the agents onto ZoomInfo’s Agentic Platform. You will work with the Principal AI Engineer who owns the benchmark harness and productionization, the product manager who owns evaluation and policy, and the company and person engineering teams that own the pipelines the agents feed. You will not be the only person who can do this work; you will be the second, so that neither of you is a single point of failure.
This is a role for someone who has shipped LLM systems in production with evaluations, builds platform for other people to operate, and can work inside a large-scale data pipeline. You should be as comfortable writing an adapter with a replayable store and a kill switch as you are reading a miss analysis with a product manager, and you should like that the prototype you take to production was built by a PM who commits code.
What You’ll Do
Run the benchmark and golden-gate system. Move judge runs, golden-gate results, arms scorecards, and cost per record from a laptop to a scheduled system against staging. Every agent version is gated automatically, with variance and drift tracked per release. The evaluation product manager sets the thresholds; you make them enforceable.
Complete the entity-agent pipeline. Build the stages that do not exist yet: enricher fan-out, location sets, and hierarchy batch files. Migrate the classifiers to the shared runner with the Principal AI Engineer so they run at production scale. Measure throughput and unit cost per stage on named cohorts, so the cost model comes from instrumentation rather than estimates.
Build the evidence adapters. Registries, live web, mail-tenant signals, and external research vendors all sit behind one envelope with a replayable vendor store, measured lift per shape, a per-vendor kill switch, and at least two sources per shape. Vendors are swappable by design.

You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited.

Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst

Security of site automation: engineer the controls on automated vehicles, robots and similar machines that move hardware or work inside secure areas: identity and access, network isolation, what they may record and where it goes, fail-secure behavior, their place in chain of custody, and acceptance before they enter a site
Regulatory and site constraints: establish what we may sense, fly, drive, record and retain at each site, partner-operated sites included, under the aviation, spectrum, privacy and safety rules that apply there, with the waivers and approvals that extend it and coordination with local authorities set up before it is needed
Health monitoring: define and test heartbeats, loss-of-coverage and lost-link alarms and fail-secure behavior, so a silent sensor or machine shows as a fault, not a quiet day

title: Network Officer
description:
Role Summary
Insta Telecom is seeking a skilled and motivated Network Officer to join its Technical and Network Operations team in Kabul.
The Network Officer will be responsible for planning, deploying, configuring, monitoring, maintaining, and troubleshooting wireless Point-to-Point (PTP), Point-to-Multipoint (PTMP), and Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) network infrastructure.
The successful candidate will conduct technical site surveys, manage customer installations and service activations, maintain network reliability, troubleshoot connectivity issues, and coordinate with the NOC, Fiber, FTTH, and Engineering teams to ensure efficient network operations and high-quality internet services.
The position also involves supervising field technicians, preparing technical reports, supporting network expansion projects, and ensuring compliance with company technical standards and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

Duties and Responsibilities
Wireless Network Deployment (PTP/PTMP)
· Conduct technical site surveys for PTP and PTMP wireless network installations and prepare feasibility assessment reports.
· Plan, install, configure, align, test, and commission wireless links according to company standards.
· Perform wireless link performance testing, signal optimization, and connectivity verification.
· Manage customer installation activities from initial survey to final service activation.
· Support network expansion, customer migrations, and equipment upgrades.
Network Monitoring & Troubleshooting
· Monitor network performance, connectivity, signal quality, bandwidth utilization, and service stability.
· Diagnose and resolve wireless network faults, connectivity interruptions, and service degradation.
· Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on wireless radios, network equipment, and customer connections.
· Configure, troubleshoot, and maintain wireless devices and associated networking equipment.
· Ensure network availability, service reliability, and compliance with agreed SLAs.
FTTH & GPON Network Support
· Troubleshoot FTTH network connectivity and customer service issues.
· Diagnose and resolve GPON, OLT, ONT, and fiber-related faults.
· Coordinate with the Fiber and FTTH teams for service restoration and new customer activations.
· Support the installation, testing, and activation of FTTH customer connections.
Documentation & Reporting
· Prepare and maintain site survey reports, installation records, network diagrams, and maintenance documentation.
· Maintain accurate records of network configurations, customer installations, and technical changes.
· Prepare technical incident reports and provide regular updates on assigned activities.
Team Coordination & Supervision
· Coordinate with NOC, Fiber, FTTH, and Engineering teams to resolve technical issues and complete network deployments.
· Supervise and provide technical guidance to field technicians and junior network engineers.
· Support technical training and knowledge sharing among team members.
· Follow company policies, safety procedures, and technical standards.
· Perform other network-related duties assigned by the CTO or management.

Job Requirements
Education
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Telecommunications, Network Engineering, or a related field.
Relevant technical diplomas with strong practical experience may also be considered.
Professional Experience
Minimum 2–3 years of practical experience in ISP network operations, wireless network deployment, or telecommunications.
Hands-on experience installing, configuring, and troubleshooting PTP and PTMP wireless networks.
Experience in customer premises equipment (CPE) installation and internet service activation.
Experience with FTTH/GPON networks is highly desirable.
Technical Skills
Strong understanding of TCP/IP networking, IP addressing, subnetting, VLANs, routing, and switching.
Practical experience with wireless networking technologies, including PTP and PTMP systems.
Familiarity with equipment from vendors such as Ubiquiti, MikroTik, and Cambium Networks.
Ability to perform wireless site surveys, antenna alignment, signal analysis, and link optimization.
Understanding of wireless frequency planning, interference, signal strength, and link capacity.
Knowledge of PPPoE, DHCP, DNS, NAT, and basic network troubleshooting.
Familiarity with GPON technologies, OLTs, ONTs, and FTTH infrastructure.
Ability to troubleshoot fiber connectivity and optical signal issues.
Knowledge of network monitoring tools and troubleshooting utilities.
Ability to prepare technical documentation and network diagrams.
Certifications (Preferred)
CCNA (Cisco Certified Network Associate).
MikroTik MTCNA or equivalent.
Ubiquiti or Cambium wireless networking certifications.
Other relevant networking certifications are an advantage.

Alloy is where you belong!

Check out our investors and read more about us here .
About the team
The Technical Support Engineer 2 (TSE2), Triage & Discovery is the front line of Alloy’s technical support experience. This role is responsible for engaging customers early, clarifying the true issue, gathering the right technical and business context, and preparing high-quality handoffs to senior Technical Support Engineers for deeper investigation and resolution. You’ll also directly resolve repeatable, well-defined support workflows—like implementation tasks and standard configurations—giving you meaningful ownership alongside your triage work.
This isn’t a role where you passively route tickets. You’ll dig into each request, ask sharp questions, get on short calls when it’ll move things faster, and build a clear picture of what’s actually going on. The best person for this role is someone who’s energized by customer interaction, comfortable navigating technical systems, and skilled at turning ambiguity into clarity. By improving the quality of initial problem discovery, you’ll help the entire support organization resolve issues faster, more accurately, and with less wasted effort.
Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. We look to foster collaboration and community by having our local employees onsite three days a week, and remote employees onsite once a quarter.
What you'll be doing
As a Technical Support Engineer 2, you will be responsible for triaging incoming support cases, leading customer discovery conversations, building high-quality handoffs for senior engineers, and directly resolving straightforward tickets—all using our ticketing system, Zendesk. You’ll be leveraging your technical skills, problem-solving instincts, written communication, and verbal skills to clarify customer issues and build trust with professionalism and empathy.
Responsibilities
Serve as the first technical point of contact for incoming support requests—respond quickly, ask targeted follow-up questions, and build a clear understanding of what the customer actually needs.
Get on short customer calls (15–30 minutes) when written back-and-forth isn’t getting to the heart of the issue fast enough. Lead these calls effectively, keeping them focused on discovery and triage.
Gather the evidence that matters—logs, screenshots, timestamps, configuration details, reproduction steps—so that the next person to touch the ticket can hit the ground running.
Write clean, structured internal notes and handoffs. When you route a ticket to a senior engineer, they should be able to start solving immediately without redoing your work.
Directly resolve straightforward product questions, technical clarifications, and clearly documented support tasks, including repeatable implementation workflows managed asynchronously over days or weeks.
Diagnose issues related to Alloy’s dashboard, APIs, and integrations using logs, system tools, and debugging methods, exercising judgment about when to resolve vs. when to escalate.
Maintain accurate ticket hygiene, timely follow-ups, clear statuses, and deliver within established service level agreements (SLAs).

Role Summary
The IT Officer – MIS System Support will be responsible for the day-to-day administration, maintenance, security, and operational support of the Aurum MFI MIS system. The successful candidate will serve as the dedicated technical focal point for the system, ensuring its availability, data integrity, proper user access management, timely backups, and effective coordination with relevant departments, software developers, and external technical support providers.

Duties and Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities
1. MIS System Administration
Manage and monitor the day-to-day operation of the Aurum MFI MIS system.
Create, configure, update, suspend, and deactivate user accounts based on authorized requests.
Assign and manage user roles and access permissions in accordance with approved policies.
Maintain system configurations, operational settings, and user access records.
Monitor system performance and report technical issues, errors, or operational disruptions.
2. Data Backup and Recovery
Perform and monitor regular backups of the MIS database and related system data.
Verify backup completion and periodically test data restoration procedures.
Maintain backup logs and ensure backups are stored securely in accordance with the approved backup policy.
Coordinate with the relevant technical team to resolve backup failures and support data recovery when required.
Help ensure data integrity, availability, and business continuity.
3. Technical Support and Troubleshooting
Provide first-level technical support to MIS users and resolve routine system-related issues.
Investigate system errors, access problems, data discrepancies, and performance issues.
Document incidents, follow up on unresolved issues, and escalate complex technical problems to the relevant developers or service providers.
Coordinate system troubleshooting, bug fixes, upgrades, patches, and technical improvements.
Support system testing and verification before changes are implemented in the production environment.
4. System Maintenance and Security
Coordinate routine system maintenance and monitor system availability.
Ensure that user access is properly authorized and reviewed periodically.
Follow approved information security, data protection, and access control procedures.
Maintain technical documentation, system configuration records, backup logs, and incident reports.
Identify potential operational and security risks and report them to the relevant team.
5. Technical and Departmental Coordination
Act as the primary IT focal point for MIS-related matters.
Coordinate with the Microfinance Operations team, Finance, relevant business units, software developers, and external technical support providers.
Follow up on reported issues, requested changes, system enhancements, and pending technical tasks.
Assist in gathering business requirements and communicating them to the technical team.
6. Reporting and User Support
Prepare periodic reports on system availability, incidents, backup status, user administration, and maintenance activities.
Maintain an updated record of users, permissions, technical issues, and system changes.
Guide and assist staff in using the MIS system correctly and securely.
Provide basic user training and prepare user guides or operational instructions when necessary.
Perform other relevant IT and MIS support duties assigned by the IT Manager.

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in IT support, MIS support or a similar position.
Experience supporting a Management Information System (MIS), preferably in microfinance, banking, financial services, or another regulated organization.
Understanding of user administration, role-based access control, system security, and data protection.
Familiarity with web-based applications, application troubleshooting, and software maintenance.
Good documentation, reporting, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical teams.
Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and maintain confidentiality when handling financial and customer data.

Technical troubleshooting and analytical thinking.
Accuracy and attention to detail.
Accountability and ownership of assigned responsibilities.
Effective communication and teamwork.
Confidentiality and professional integrity.
Proactive monitoring and timely reporting of technical issues.

description:
Job Summary
Position Summary: Ariana Medical Complex invites qualified individual IT professionals and eligible IT companies or service providers to apply for the management and support of the hospital’s information technology systems.
The selected individual or service provider will be responsible for planning, managing, maintaining, securing, and improving the hospital’s IT infrastructure and services. These services must support the hospital’s clinical, administrative, financial, and operational activities while ensuring system reliability, information security, confidentiality of patient data, and continuity of essential hospital services.
Applicants may apply under one of the following categories:
Category A – Individual IT Manager: An experienced IT professional responsible for managing the hospital’s IT operations and supervising the hospital’s IT staff.
Category B – IT Company / Service Provider: A qualified company that provides IT management services through a designated IT manager and an appropriately skilled technical team under an agreement with the hospital.
Key Responsibilities:
A. Strategic Leadership and IT Governance
Develop and implement an IT strategy aligned with the hospital’s objectives and healthcare service requirements.
Establish, review, and maintain IT policies, procedures, technical standards, and operational controls.
Advise hospital management on technology investments, digital transformation, system improvements, and IT-related risks.
Develop an annual IT work plan, including priorities, resource requirements, maintenance schedules, and improvement activities.
Ensure IT operations support the hospital’s clinical, administrative, financial, and operational departments.
B. IT Operations and Infrastructure
Manage and maintain servers, computer networks, databases, applications, workstations, printers, scanners, switches, cameras, and related equipment.
Ensure the availability, performance, reliability, and proper functioning of critical hospital IT systems.
Manage network architecture, routing, connectivity, wireless networks, internet services, email systems, and internal communications.
Coordinate installation, configuration, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of IT equipment.
Maintain an updated inventory of IT equipment, software, licenses, systems, and related assets.
Minimize service interruptions and coordinate timely resolution of technical problems.
C. Information Security and Data Protection
Protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of hospital information and patient records.
Implement appropriate access controls, user account management, password policies, endpoint protection, and security monitoring.
Establish and maintain regular data backup, restoration testing, disaster recovery, and business continuity procedures.
Monitor and address cybersecurity risks, vulnerabilities, unauthorized access, malware, and other security incidents.
Ensure that access to patient information is restricted to authorized personnel and permitted purposes.
Report significant security incidents promptly to the designated hospital authority.
Ensure that hospital data is not copied, transferred, disclosed, or used without proper authorization.
D. Systems Development and Improvement
Assess, recommend, install, configure, and maintain suitable hardware, software, and technology solutions.
Support the effective operation and improvement of hospital information systems, including clinical, administrative, financial, and other approved platforms.
Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend cost-effective solutions that improve hospital services.
Coordinate system upgrades, software updates, equipment replacement, and technical projects.
Ensure that changes to critical systems are properly authorized, documented, tested, and implemented.
E. IT Support and Team Management
Provide or coordinate timely technical support to all hospital departments.
Supervise, guide, and evaluate hospital IT staff, where applicable.
Ensure proper allocation of IT duties, technical coverage, staff development, and performance monitoring.
Establish a system for receiving, recording, prioritizing, tracking, and resolving IT support requests.
Provide advanced technical assistance for complex IT and system-related issues.
Maintain appropriate technical coverage for critical hospital services, including agreed arrangements for urgent and after-hours support.
F. Budget, Procurement, and Vendor Management
Prepare or contribute to the annual IT budget, equipment replacement plan, and maintenance requirements.
Recommend cost-effective procurement of IT equipment, software, licenses, and technical services.
Coordinate with authorized hospital departments regarding procurement specifications, vendor evaluation, and technical acceptance.
Manage technical relationships with internet providers, software vendors, equipment suppliers, and other service providers.
Monitor vendor performance, warranties, service agreements, licenses, and maintenance commitments.
Ensure that procurement and expenditure recommendations are submitted through the hospital’s approved authorization procedures.
G. Compliance, Documentation, and Reporting
Ensure compliance with hospital policies, applicable regulations, accreditation requirements, and approved information security procedures.
Maintain updated technical documentation, network diagrams, system configurations, equipment inventories, access records, and maintenance logs.
Prepare regular reports covering system availability, support requests, incidents, cybersecurity risks, completed activities, and proposed improvements.
Report major risks, service disruptions, resource gaps, and unresolved technical issues to the designated hospital authority.
Perform other relevant duties assigned by hospital leadership within the approved scope of work.
2. Confidentiality and Ownership of Hospital Information
The selected individual or company must:
Sign the required confidentiality and data protection undertaking before receiving access to hospital systems or information.
Use hospital data and systems solely for authorized purposes.
Maintain appropriate safeguards for patient information, employee records, financial information, and other confidential hospital data.
Refrain from retaining, disclosing, transferring, or using hospital information after termination of the engagement, except where expressly authorized or legally required.
Ensure that all hospital data, configurations, documentation, credentials, and other hospital-owned information remain under the hospital’s control.

Role Summary
Ummat International Hospital is seeking a qualified, motivated, and responsible ICT and HMIS Officer to provide general information technology support and ensure the effective management, monitoring, and utilization of the hospital's Hospital Management Information System (HMIS).

In addition, the officer will oversee the daily operation and effective use of the existing HMIS, provide technical support to users, monitor data quality, and train hospital staff on the proper use of the system.

Duties and Responsibilities
A. Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
Provide routine technical support for computers, printers, scanners, and other IT equipment used within the hospital.
Troubleshoot basic hardware, software, operating system, and network connectivity issues.
Assist with the installation, configuration, and maintenance of authorized software and IT equipment.
Support internet connectivity and local area network (LAN) operations and coordinate with service providers to resolve major technical issues.
Assist hospital staff with common IT-related problems and provide basic guidance on the appropriate use of IT equipment and applications.

Manage, monitor, and support the daily operation and effective utilization of the hospital's existing HMIS.
Ensure that relevant hospital departments use the HMIS correctly and consistently in their daily activities.
Provide training, guidance, and ongoing technical support to hospital staff on the proper use of the HMIS.
Monitor the accuracy, completeness, and timely entry of information into the system.
Identify HMIS-related technical and operational problems, resolve issues within the scope of responsibility, and coordinate with the relevant technical team or service provider when necessary.
Monitor HMIS user accounts and access permissions in accordance with assigned roles and responsibilities.
Support the generation, review, and preparation of hospital reports using information available in the HMIS.

Identify gaps in HMIS utilization and recommend practical measures to improve system use and operational efficiency.

Bachelor's degree in information and communication technology (ICT), Information Technology (IT), Computer Science, or a related field.

Ability to provide technical support and train staff with different levels of computer literacy.
Good understanding of data quality, information security, user access control, and patient data confidentiality.
Ability to prepare basic technical records and support the generation of HMIS reports.
Strong communication, coordination, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively with different hospital departments.

HMIS operation, management, and monitoring.
HMIS user support and staff training.
Data quality monitoring and reporting.
Information security and confidentiality.
Communication, coordination, and teamwork.

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.
Discord seeks a seasoned Data Engineer, focusing on our advertising product data. In this role, you will drive technical vision and strategy for ads data engineering in support of our ML initiatives while building and maintaining sophisticated data pipelines, datasets, and analytical tools. You will lead cross-functional initiatives to transform our advertising products through data-driven insights and mentor fellow engineers to deliver exceptional results.
This role works heavily with Data Science, Machine Learning, and product. If leading technical innovation, architecting scalable solutions, and empowering teams through data excites you, we encourage you to make a move!
What You'll Be Doing
Design and own core ads data models : fact/dim tables, canonical datasets, and aggregation layers that power delivery, measurement, targeting, attribution, and ML use cases.
Build and maintain the ML data that enables ads ranking, delivery, and targeting - including feature development, label generation workflows, intra-day training, and ML input observability to catch data quality issues before they degrade model performance.
Build conversion measurement pipelines and integrate third-party attribution data - including Conversion Attribution and Mobile Measurement Partner (MMP) integrations (Adjust, AppsFlyer, Singular) - ensuring attribution accuracy and data parity across measurement surfaces.
Build batch and near real-time pipeline infrastructure across the ads ecosystem - pushing toward lower-latency data for ML and reporting use cases on our BigQuery + dbt + Dagster stack. Partnering with Data Platform on launch and success of new data processing engines to support low latency requirements..
Develop data quality frameworks, monitoring systems, automated anomaly detection, and SLA infrastructure for critical ads pipelines at massive scale.
Proactively identify foundational data infrastructure gaps - including those with broad implications across ML, measurement, and reporting - and design scalable, canonical solutions that multiple teams can depend on.
Build systems from scratch in a rapidly evolving, greenfield advertising data environment - making sound architectural decisions with incomplete information and balancing short-term delivery with long-term infrastructure investment.
Drive alignment across Data Science, ML Engineering, Ads Product, and GTM teams through clear narratives that connect data infrastructure decisions to business outcomes and revenue impact.
Mentor engineers through technical challenges, code and design reviews, and ownership of complex projects - contributing to the culture and engineering standards of the Data Engineering team team.
What you should have
5+ years of hands-on experience writing production code and architecting data pipelines with high-volume consumer data in advertising technology domains (ad delivery, ranking, targeting, identity, conversion measurement).
Deep expertise in digital advertising data engineering - specifically in ads delivery, conversion measurement, attribution pipelines, or ML feature data infrastructure. Experience with Conversion Data and APIs, MMP integrations, or identity graph infrastructure is strongly valued.
Demonstrated experience building data models in a greenfield or 0-to-1 environment where requirements change frequently, documentation is sparse, and architectural decisions are made with incomplete information.
Expert-level SQL and Python . Strong ability to design performant, maintainable data models and write production-quality pipeline code.

Platform owns the foundation the company runs on: compute and deployment, reliability and on-call, CI/CD and monorepo health, developer environments, the infrastructure that model training and inference run on, and the security boundaries around all of it.
AI and agent tooling is the clearest example. You will contribute to how models are trained and served here, as well as how agents work inside our codebase: the environments they run in, the verification that makes their output trustworthy, and the review paths that keep it all legible. There is no industry standard and you’ll help form our opinions rather than inheriting one.
Our users are other engineers. Expect to spend time with all the other engineering teams, understanding their needs and building a roadmap. The scope is large, so you'll be choosing what to leave alone as much as build.
Architecture decisions here last: this is a small team covering a large surface. You'll have real room to decide things, and you'll stay close to the systems you decide about.
What you'll own
Own our platform: GCP, Kubernetes, Temporal, the GPU fleet behind cloud export, and the deploy and rollback machinery everything ships through. You'll be in the on-call rotation, and we'll expect you to make it quieter and more actionable.
The AI enablement substrate: GPU capacity, training and inference pipelines, and the reliability and cost of the systems serving models in production.
Cost is an engineering constraint: infrastructure decisions have a number attached and you're expected to make smart trade-offs. As inference grows with usage, the metering and attribution behind those numbers sit with this team.
Security comes with the systems you run : identity and access, secrets management, least-privilege boundaries, and supply-chain integrity.
Make what you build legible. Infrastructure-as-code that explains itself. Runbooks and in-repo context written for someone jumping in to help. Observability that tells you what failed and why.
Improve how the team learns and ships. Form hypotheses, instrument your work, release incrementally, and read results honestly. Strengthen the tooling, standards, tests, observability, and release practices that help the team move quickly without compromising quality.

You've run systems where failure was expensive, and your opinions about reliability and deployment come from consequences rather than reading.

You've found important unowned work, scoped it, earned buy-in, and delivered it without being handed a spec.
You build a minimal repro, read the logs, and write targeted checks to prove a fix works instead of trusting output.

GPU and ML infrastructure: capacity planning, training or inference pipelines, serving cost and latency. If you haven't run a GPU fleet, experience with expensive capacity-constrained systems transfers well.

title: ML Inference Engineer – Terminal-Bench Task Designer
description:
Headquarters:
Overview
We are building a benchmark that tests how well AI agents handle real expert work in a terminal. We are hiring ML inference and serving experts to turn real, paid tasks from their jobs into expert-level Terminal-Bench challenges. Each task includes the environment, a working solution, and an automated check that proves the result is correct.
***THIS IS A TASK BASED COMPENSATION MODEL. PLEASE CHECK THE APPLICATION QUESTIONS FOR MORE DETAILS.***
Responsibilities
• Design expert-level Terminal-Bench tasks that turn real, paid ML inference work from your own experience into challenges an AI agent must solve end to end.
• Define the files, systems and environments each task runs on, such as model serving with streaming, so the challenge is realistic, reproducible and command-line solvable.
• Write a working reference solution for every task and verify it runs end to end, sized for about 60 to 75 minutes of expert effort.
• Build automated checks that objectively prove a result is correct, including cases where ML outputs go wrong silently, such as numerical drift or metric bugs.
• Package tasks with Docker and Git so they are reproducible, and document the systems, tools, data and rules involved so reviewers can validate difficulty.
• Iterate on tasks based on reviewer feedback and agent test runs, adjusting difficulty and fixing ambiguities so each task stays expert-level, fair and objectively gradable.

• 3+ years doing ML inference or serving work hands-on (not only studying, selling or managing it), or a PhD plus active research in the subfield
• Did this work in the last 3 years and can name the systems, tools, data and rules used
• Trained, served or evaluated models at real scale (multi-GPU or production serving), not only notebooks or API calls
• Hands-on with PyTorch or JAX internals and serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM
• Can explain how ML results go wrong without errors (numerical drift, metric bugs) and how to catch them
• Technical fluency in Python and the command line, and with files, CSV/JSON, APIs or databases
• Availability to start by early November 2026 and complete tasks of about 60 to 75 minutes each
Nice-to-have

• Contributions to PyTorch, vLLM or SGLang
• GPU profiling experience
• Docker and Git proficiency
• Experience writing automated tests

description:
We’re looking for an incredible senior engineer to help us build the future of blockchain scalability.
This is an ideal opportunity for an engineer who is already passionate about tackling problems in blockchain scalability, or looking to break into the blockchain engineering space. If you’re looking to work in a fast-paced, high-impact team and help shape the direction of our product and company, this position is for you.

Caldera enables dynamic, scalable blockchain experiences. Currently, dapps that are deployed to general-purpose blockchain compete with thousands of other applications for space on the network. This can lead to congestion and high fees or even network outages.
That’s where we come in. We’re building software that makes it easy for the most innovative blockchain applications to launch their own ultra-performant blockchains (rollups), enabling applications to own their ecosystem, scale to millions of users, and provide a superior user experience to their users. We already operate chains for a significant user base, and are eager to expand that operation with a sleek, performant team.
As a Senior Infrastructure Engineer at Caldera , you will:

Expand and hone our DevOps pipeline, allowing blockchains to be deployed and operated reliably and securely
Continuously improving the observability stack for the services we provide
Maintain and enhance the security posture of our infrastructure in AWS and Kubernetes, and upwards in the stack for the apps we run.

title: Security Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Shopware ist ein führendes E-Commerce-System , das es Unternehmen weltweit ermöglicht, im digitalen Handel schnell und effizient zu skalieren. Als zukunftsweisende Open-Source-Lösung wird Shopware bereits von einigen der größten europäischen Marken, Einzelhändlern und Herstellern im B2C- und B2B-Bereich eingesetzt.
Hilf dabei, Shopware-Produkte sicherer zu machen, indem du während der gesamten Produktentwicklung Sicherheitsrisiken aufdeckst und reduzierst. Du arbeitest mit den Produktentwicklungsteams daran, Schwachstellen zu untersuchen, sichere Konzepte und Tests zu verbessern und praxisnahe Maßnahmen aufzubauen, die wiederkehrende Probleme in Commerce Core, Services und angrenzenden Produktbereichen verhindern.
Product Security Engineering ist eine Engineering-Funktion . Die Produktteams bleiben dafür verantwortlich, ihren eigenen Code zu korrigieren und zu testen. Dieses Team bringt gezielte Sicherheitsexpertise, eine gemeinsame Roadmap zur Prävention und eine klare Koordination für produktübergreifende Sicherheitsarbeit ein.
Requirements
Untersuche Schwachstellenmeldungen, Sicherheitswarnungen, interne Findings und Nacharbeiten zu Sicherheitsvorfällen . Bewerte die technischen Auswirkungen und unterstütze dabei, bestätigte Aufgaben an die zuständigen Product Owner weiterzuleiten.
Arbeite direkt mit Entwicklerinnen und Entwicklern an sicherem Design, Threat Models, Code Reviews, Ursachenanalysen, Fixes und Regressionstests für besonders risikoreiche Produktbereiche.
Entwickle und verbessere wiederverwendbare Sicherheitskontrollen , Leitfäden für Entwicklerinnen und Entwickler, Tests für Missbrauchsszenarien und praxisnahe Automatisierung zur Erkennung und Behebung von Schwachstellen.
Unterstütze dabei, für Product-Security-Findings klare Verantwortlichkeiten, Schweregrade, Reaktionsziele, betroffene Versionen und Nachweise zum Abschluss festzuhalten.
Arbeite mit den Engineering-Teams von Commerce Core und Services an Sicherheitsaufgaben über verschiedene Repositories, unterstützte Versionen, APIs, Integrationen und das Extension-Ökosystem hinweg .
Unterstütze koordinierte Sicherheits-Releases : Ermittle betroffene Bereiche, prüfe technische Behebungen und stimme dich mit Engineering, Product Operations, Quality, InfoSec und DevRel ab.
Überführe Erkenntnisse aus Sicherheitsvorfällen und Releases in konkrete Änderungen am Engineering, Tests oder Tools. Verfolge anschließend nach, ob diese Maßnahmen übernommen werden.
Kommuniziere bei zeitkritischen Aufgaben klar und dokumentiere Entscheidungen in den vereinbarten GitHub- und Confluence-Einträgen, damit Teams den Status nicht aus Slack-Verläufen rekonstruieren müssen.
Wirke an gemeinsamen Teampraktiken mit und vertrete bei Bedarf den anderen Produktbereich.
Das bringst du mit:
Fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und Interesse an Produkt- oder Anwendungssicherheit.
Praktische Kenntnisse typischer Risiken in der Anwendungssicherheit , etwa Schwachstellen bei Authentifizierung und Autorisierung, Zugriffskontrolle, Datentrennung, API-Sicherheit, Umgang mit Zugangsdaten, Injection und Abhängigkeiten.
Die Fähigkeit, produktiven Code und Tests zu lesen und zu ändern , Risiken für Entwicklerinnen und Entwickler verständlich zu erklären und wartbare Fixes mit umzusetzen.
Erfahrung mit Threat Modeling, Sicherheitstests, Schwachstellenanalysen oder Secure Code Reviews ; in einigen Bereichen bringst du fundiertes Wissen mit, in anderen möchtest du dich weiterentwickeln.
Gutes Urteilsvermögen bei der Einschätzung von Schweregrad, Auswirkungen auf Kundinnen und Kunden und Ausnutzbarkeit sowie bei der Frage, wann ein Problem sofort eskaliert werden muss.
Klare schriftliche Kommunikation und die Fähigkeit, bei unklaren oder dringenden Aufgaben teamübergreifend zusammenzuarbeiten.
Kenntnisse von PHP sowie mit Shopwares Produkten, Services oder dem Extension-Ökosystem sind hilfreich.

Als Cloud Engineer liegt dein Schwerpunkt auf der Implementierung moderner Data- und AI-Infrastrukturen, wobei du GPU-Cluster orchestrierst, Datenplattformen strukturierst und Pipelines für ein effizientes Modell-Training sowie den stabilen Betrieb von Inferenz-Schnittstellen automatisierst.
Datenplattformen konzipierst du, von der Storage-Architektur über Lakehouse-Formate bis zur Integration von Orchestrierung und Streaming-Komponenten.
Tools wie Airflow, Spark on Kubernetes oder Ray setzt du auf, integrierst sie miteinander und stellst sicher, dass Data- und ML-Workflows zuverlässig in Produktion laufen.
Infrastructure-as-Code und GitOps sind für dich der Standard. Bei sensiblen Datenprodukten baust du Sicherheit von Beginn an ein, von Network Policies bis zu den Anforderungen aus der Data Governance.
Monitoring, Incident-Handling und GPU-Kapazitätsplanung liegen in deiner Verantwortung.

AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, StackIT, Kubernetes
Terraform, ArgoCD, Helm, Cilium, Kyverno
Airflow, Spark, Kafka, Ray, Kueue
Databricks, Snowflake, dbt, Iceberg
S3, PostgreSQL, pgvector, MLflow, vLLM, KServe
Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry
Python, Go

Wer gut zu uns passen würde
Ob du ein Studium oder eine Ausbildung im IT-Bereich abgeschlossen hast, ist für uns nebensächlich. Für uns zählen deine fachlichen Skills und deine Persönlichkeit:
Du hast fundierte Kubernetes-Erfahrung im produktiven Betrieb und bringst tiefgehende Kenntnisse im Umgang mit einem der großen Cloud-Provider (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, StackIT) mit.

title: Backend Engineer Internship
description:
Overview: Supply Chain API and Microservices Development
The Backend Engineer is a hands-on role responsible for the development, scaling, and maintenance of the core API services that power our entire integrated platform. You will build highly reliable, secure, and performant backend services within the NestJS modular monolith, focusing on critical supply chain logic, complex payment integrations, and the orchestration backbone for our AI agents.
Internship Details
Duration: 3 months
Start Date: Immediate
Location: Remote
Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.
Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will own the backend development for the most complex domain logic, ensuring scalability and transactional integrity.
API Development & Implementation: Design, develop, and deploy highly scalable APIs for all platform components using Node.js 22 and NestJS within the TypeScript modular monolith. This includes the backends for the e-commerce checkout, internal tool APIs, and the B2B portal.
SCM Domain Logic: Implement complex, transactional business logic within the core supply chain modules: Order Management (OMS), Warehouse Management (WMS), and Manufacturing Execution (MES). Ensure data integrity using PostgreSQL 15.
Integrations & Payments: Implement secure, reliable integrations with third-party payment gateways and external shipping/logistics providers.
Performance & Reliability: Implement effective caching strategies using Redis to boost API performance. Design and implement asynchronous processing and event-driven workflows to ensure system reliability and handle high-volume operations.
Security & Monitoring: Ensure all services adhere to security standards (JWT authorization, API security). Integrate backend services with the observability stack (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Loki) for monitoring and tracing.
Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must possess deep, hands-on experience with our core backend and data stack:
Core Backend: Expert proficiency in Node.js 22, NestJS, and TypeScript (mandatory).
Data Layer: Strong expertise in PostgreSQL 15 (schema design, query optimization) and utilizing Redis for caching.
Architecture: Experience designing and implementing APIs (REST/GraphQL), asynchronous communication, and event-driven patterns.
Workflow: Experience working within a Monorepo structure, contributing to CI/CD via Makefile, and utilizing Docker for local development.
AI Agent Focus
You will build the reliable, secure services required for AI agent orchestration.
Agent Orchestration: Develop the backend services and API endpoints necessary to securely orchestrate, manage, and scale the AI agent systems.
Data Access Services: Implement secure, high-performance services that allow AI agents (using frameworks like LangChain) to access and write necessary data to the WMS/OMS modules without compromising transactional integrity.
Success Metrics & Career Path
Performance will be measured by:
Service Reliability: Uptime and stability of deployed services, achieving defined SLOs.
Code Quality & Efficiency: Delivery of clean, well-tested, and performant code that scales effectively.
Feature Velocity: Timely and efficient delivery of complex backend features, particularly within the critical OMS and WMS modules.
Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Technical Architect or Engineering Lead, working directly with Frontend, QA, and SRE teams to deliver high-quality supply chain functionality.

What We're Looking For
- 5+ years as a systems administrator, endpoint engineer or similar, including at least 2 years packaging and deploying software at scale (Intune, SCCM/ConfigMgr, Jamf, Munki, Chocolatey, winget or similar)
- Hands-on Windows packaging: MSI, EXE and MSIX installers, silent switches, detection rules, per-user vs. per-machine installs, x64/arm64
- Hands-on macOS packaging: PKG and DMG, app bundles and bundle IDs, universal vs. architecture-specific builds

- Experience automating deployments through pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or similar), not only through a management console

- You diagnose failed installs from logs, exit codes and metadata, on devices you can't access
- You can reverse-engineer poorly documented installers, find stable download URLs and version sources, and recognize when an app can't be packaged (login, paywall, bot protection) and write down why
- Maintaining packages in public repositories (winget-pkgs, Chocolatey Community, Homebrew Cask, AutoPkg)
- Python or Go, AWS, vulnerability/CVE data, VM-based install testing
- Strong written English for an async-first team
Own the end-to-end delivery and reliability of third-party application packages across Windows and macOS, from installer analysis and automated validation to production patching. Combine deep packaging expertise with scripting, TypeScript, CI/CD, and AI-assisted engineering to ship applications while continuously improving the automation behind the catalog.

Honest, simple, and transparent culture

title: Remote Senior Software Engineer, (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor)
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

title: Remote Python Senior Software Engineer, AI Training
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

title: Staff Network Engineer (AI Infrastructure)
description:
As a Staff Network Engineer at vCluster Labs , you aren't just configuring switches; you are building the automation logic that configures them. AI Clouds run on InfiniBand and high-speed Ethernet fabrics that most teams still wire up by hand, one customer at a time. You will build the automation that turns that fabric into repeatable provisioning logic. You start in a small R&D group alongside our CTO and grow into owning this area as it becomes a core part of our platform.
As a Staff Network Engineer, your role will include:
Fabric automation: You will design and build the systems that automatically provision and configure NVIDIA switches and InfiniBand fabrics, including integration with NVIDIA UFM. Manual, per-customer switch setup is the thing you are replacing.
Network config management and sync: You will build the control loop that keeps switch, VLAN, and VXLAN state consistent with what our platform intends, detects drift, and reconciles it safely in production.
NAT gateway and L4 load balancing: You will build the gateway and load balancing layer that tenant clusters depend on for connectivity, with failover designed in from day one rather than bolted on later.
Scale and failure engineering: You will define how our network layer behaves at large scale: BGP route table limits, convergence, failover, and what happens when a link, switch, or gateway dies under real AI workloads.
Customer Zero for AI networking: You will run your automation on real AI Cloud environments, bring back what breaks, and turn hard-won operational lessons into product behavior our customers never have to think about.
Technical direction: You will help decide what we build versus integrate with partner solutions, write the design and requirements docs, and set the standards for how networking works across vCluster products.
This role could be a fit for you if you bring:
You have built network automation, not just operated networks: You have shipped software that configures switches, routers, or load balancers programmatically, ideally as part of a product or internal platform other teams relied on.
NVIDIA networking experience: Hands-on work with NVIDIA UFM, NVIDIA Spectrum or Quantum switches, Cumulus Linux, or NVUE, including programming against their APIs.
Deep fabric fundamentals: Strong command of InfiniBand, VLAN, VXLAN and EVPN, and BGP, including how they behave and fail at production scale.
Production scale scars: You have run networks at real production scale, seen them break, and helped fix the root cause with automation rather than runbooks.
Software engineering ability: You write production code in Go or Python, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and think of network config as code.
Bonus points for:
AI networking depth: Experience tuning fabrics for GPU training or inference workloads, such as RoCEv2, congestion control, rail-optimized topologies, or Spectrum-X.
AI Cloud or hyperscaler background: You helped build network automation at a GPU cloud, hyperscaler, or large CDN.
Load balancer and gateway internals: Experience building L4 load balancers or NAT gateways, including with eBPF/XDP or DPDK.

title: Senior Software Engineer, (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor)
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

Design and develop new mobile applications from the ground up for Android and iOS.
Build, maintain, and improve cross-platform applications using modern mobile development technologies.

description:

Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 300+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, annual revenue now exceeds $100m USD and millions use our browser on on Mac , Windows , iOS , and Android , our search engine , and the DuckDuckGo subscription . We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including Duck.ai , which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place. Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!
Your Team and Role
As a Senior Product Designer, Design Systems you'll be the first of its kind at DuckDuckGo. You'll take ownership of our design system at a pivotal moment, with a chance to define both a role and a roadmap from the ground up — helping build the process, not just step into one. You'll audit our existing system, lead projects that move it forward across platforms and products like Duck.ai and Search, as well as shape how we manage and scale it as we grow.
Applying your hands-on design skills, you will autonomously lead highly impactful projects that scale across millions of users, and collaborate with team members at all levels to pioneer new solutions as we build out the privacy layer for the internet. From ideation to execution, you'll assess vague problems, propose high-impact solutions, and execute them against a set of success criteria. You'll have a voice in all product-related design decisions, whether large or small, and an opportunity to work on a team dedicated to our ethical, privacy by design approach. Read more about Design at DuckDuckGo on our blog: https://spreadprivacy.com/ethical-by-design/

Ability to take initiative in generating ideas and carrying them forward with urgency and discretion, while working openly and collaboratively

title: Solution Engineer
description:
Who We Are
At RelationalAI , we’re solving one of the most important challenges in artificial intelligence: how to teach large language models the logic, semantics, and business context of the modern enterprise.
Frontier models are trained almost entirely on public data — they can speak about the world, but they don’t understand your business. We fix that.
RelationalAI has pioneered a breakthrough called Superalignment — technology that enables LLMs to learn natively from private, structured enterprise data inside the data cloud.
By combining this with relational knowledge graphs and our proprietary neuro/symbolic-relational reasoners , we deliver trustworthy decision intelligence : systems that use semantic models to truly understand how a business operates and can reason across its data to drive better outcomes.
We’re a globally distributed team of engineers, scientists, and builders redefining how AI learns from data. We believe that high-stakes decisions deserve frontier intelligence — intelligence that’s explainable, aligned, and grounded in reality.
If you’re driven by curiosity, thrive in complexity, and want to help build the system that brings true understanding to enterprise AI, you’ll feel right at home here.
The Role
You will be embedded inside our customers' hardest problems, and you will own the outcome until it works in production.
You'll sit with executives, domain experts, and data teams to find the decisions that actually move their business - inventory that's in the wrong place, risk concentrations nobody can see, fraud patterns that only emerge across three systems, capacity plans built on guesses. Then you'll model their world in our ontology, formulate the reasoning problem, write the PyRel, and ship something that runs against their real data in their own Snowflake account.
Every engagement here produces two deliverables.
The first is the one the customer sees: a working decision system that changes how they operate.
The second is the one that matters most to us: the pile of things you had to invent because our platform didn't have them yet. The modelling pattern you hand-rolled. The constraint formulation that should have been a primitive. The three-hour workaround where an API should have existed. You bring those back, you argue for them, and the strongest of them become product.
That second deliverable is why this role exists. If you only ever deliver the first one, we've hired a consultant. We're not hiring consultants.
You'll operate with unusual autonomy: you decide what's worth building, when a workaround is acceptable and when it's technical debt we'll regret, and when to tell a customer their real problem is not the one they asked about. You'll be technical enough that when something breaks in a customer environment, you find the root cause yourself rather than filing a ticket and waiting.
What You'll Do
Own outcomes end to end - discovery, modelling, implementation, performance tuning, production hardening, and the measurement that proves it worked. Not a handoff at each stage. Yours.
Build, not describe - design and ship decision solutions on our modelling, reasoning, and learning stack: ontologies over customer data, rules, graph analytics, optimisation formulations, predictive models
Fill the gaps yourself - when a customer workflow is blocked on something the platform doesn't do, scope it and build it. Then push the general version upstream: read our source, form a hypothesis before you escalate, open the PR.
Close the loop with Product - every deployment generates a signal. Bring back reproductions, patterns, and specific failure modes ("the only way I could express this was by abusing X in this way"), not vibes. You are one of the loudest inputs into our roadmap.
Run technical discovery that gets to the truth - workshops, demos, and proofs of concept designed to find out whether we can actually solve the problem, not to look impressive.

title: FinOps Engineer
description:
About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
About the Role
We're looking for a FinOps Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the Terraform or Lambda that ships the fix, working on a product feature chasing a number until it reconciles, and influencing product decisions when cost to reliability tradeoffs hit. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.
What You'll Be Responsible For
In this role, you'll:
Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.
Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.
Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review.
Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit.
Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards engineering and finance can both read.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics.
Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash
Are comfortable with cost/billing tooling: AWS Cost Explorer, Cost & Usage Reports, GCP Billing Reports, and BI/dashboarding (we use Hex).
Have experience with, or are comfortable picking up, Linear and Notion as the system of record for tracking and documenting FinOps work.
Experience with a dedicated cloud cost management platform (e.g. CloudZero, Vantage, or similar) is a plus, not required.
Can analyze cost data and present it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Have prior experience in a FinOps, cloud cost management, or cloud governance role.
Are energized by doing the unglamorous, high-leverage work (the schlep) that unblocks other teams, and by working cross-functionally without positional authority.
What We Offer
Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.
ESOP
Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.
Health Benefits
Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
